Reused classifiers may misclassify materials if the new data set does not share similar characteristics (e.g., data value ranges or material locations) [S1].

The claim is explicitly stated in the notes for Source [S1] ('Reused classifiers may misclassify materials if the new data set does not share similar characteristics (e.g., data value ranges or material locations).') and is further elaborated in the main text of Source [S1], which states: 'When reusing a trained classifier, it is necessary that the two data sets share similar characteristics. For example, if data value is used for classification, the same range of data values in two data sets should represent the same material. If position is taken into account, the materials in the different data sets should be at similar locations.' The evidence fully supports every part of the claim.
supported
